claims.source: While Astrin depleted cells displayed multipolar spindles as reported (Thein et al., 2007), cells expressing either Astrin-WT or -∆70 displayed bipolar spindles, indicating a successful rescue of the multipolar spindle phenotype seen in the absence of Astrin.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through spindle morphology analysis in Figure 2D,E.

claims.claim: The kinetochore pool of Astrin-SKAP is dispensable for bipolar spindle maintenance.
claims.source: We conclude the kinetochore pool of Astrin-SKAP is dispensable for bipolar spindle maintenance.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the observation that Astrin-∆70 mutant rescues bipolar spindle formation.

claims.claim: Cells expressing Astrin-∆70 mutant showed a delayed anaphase onset compared to Astrin-WT.
claims.source: Analysis of the time taken from Nuclear Envelope Break Down (NEBD) to anaphase onset, using YFP-Astrin signal on the spindle, showed a delayed anaphase onset in cells expressing Astrin-∆70 mutant compared to Astrin-WT
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claims.claim: Spindle bipolarity and chromosome alignment or congression were unperturbed in Astrin-∆70 mutant expressing cells.
claims.source: spindle bipolarity and chromosome alignment or congression were however unperturbed in mutant expressing cells (Figure 2F,G)
claims.evidence: This is observed in time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claims.claim: Kinetochore-bound Astrin is required for timely anaphase, but not the congression of chromosomes or the maintenance of bipolar spindles.
claims.source: In summary, kinetochore-bound Astrin is required for timely anaphase, but not the congression of chromosomes or the maintenance of bipolar spindles.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from multiple experimental observations with Astrin mutants.

claims.claim: The C-terminal tail of Astrin enables the selective recognition of end-on attached kinetochores and the timely onset of chromosome segregation.
claims.source: The C-terminal tail of Astrin enables the selective recognition of end-on attached kinetochores and the timely onset of chromosome segregation.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that the ∆70 mutant fails to enrich at kinetochores and delays anaphase.

claims.claim: A bioinformatic search identified a putative PP1-docking motif RVxF in the unstructured C-terminal tail of Astrin.
claims.source: This revealed a putative PP1-docking motif RVxF, previously reported in KNL1 (Bajaj et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is identified through bioinformatic analysis and supported by citation to previous work on PP1-docking motifs.

claims.claim: A bioinformatic search could identify Astrin elsewhere in Bilateria using the unstructured C-terminal tail.
claims.source: Importantly, using the unstructured C-terminal tail, a bioinformatic search could identify Astrin elsewhere in Bilateria (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Source data 1)
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The incidence of YFP-Astrin-4A crescents was significantly reduced compared to YFP-Astrin-WT crescents.
claims.source: The incidence of YFP-Astrin-4A crescents was significantly reduced compared to YFP-Astrin-WT crescents (Figure 3A,B; Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) in congressed kinetochores of metaphase cells
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of kinetochore localization shown in Figure 3A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: The incidence of Astrin sleeves at congressed kinetochores was significantly increased in cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A compared to YFP-Astrin-WT.
claims.source: However, the incidence of Astrin sleeves at congressed kinetochores was significantly increased in cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A compared to YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 3B)
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The RVxF motif is critical for enriching but not the initial recruitment of Astrin at the kinetochore.
claims.source: These findings show that the RVxF motif is critical for enriching but not the initial recruitment of Astrin at the kinetochore.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from observations that Astrin-4A can form sleeves but not crescents.

claims.claim: Cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A showed a striking delay in anaphase onset compared to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT.
claims.source: Tracking mitosis in YFP-Astrin-4A expressing cells treated with Astrin siRNA showed a striking delay in anaphase onset, compared to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claims.claim: The delay in anaphase onset in Astrin-4A expressing cells occurred despite the normal completion of chromosome congression at the spindle equator.
claims.source: This delay in anaphase onset was despite the normal completion of chromosome congression at the spindle equator (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is observed in time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: MG132-treated metaphase cells depleted of endogenous Astrin and expressing YFP-Astrin-4A maintained a bipolar spindle and aligned chromosomes similar to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT.
claims.source: In agreement, MG132-treated metaphase cells depleted of endogenous Astrin and expressing YFP-Astrin-4A maintained a bipolar spindle and aligned chromosomes similar to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C,D).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through fixed-cell analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C,D.

claims.claim: The PP1 docking RVxF motif is dispensable for spindle bipolarity and chromosome congression but is crucial for the enrichment of Astrin-crescents and normal timing of anaphase.
claims.source: In conclusion, the PP1 docking RVxF motif is dispensable for spindle bipolarity and chromosome congression but is crucial for the enrichment of Astrin-crescents and normal timing of anaphase.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from multiple experimental observations with the Astrin-4A mutant.

claims.claim: In Astrin-4A expressing cells, dim kinetochore-crescents gradually declined into Astrin-sleeves (referred as, blinking).
claims.source: In Astrin-4A expressing cells, dim kinetochore-crescents gradually declined into Astrin-sleeves (referred as, blinking; Figure 3E)
claims.evidence: This is observed in high-resolution time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: Astrin-WT crescents were retained brightly at congressed kinetochores.
claims.source: In contrast, Astrin-WT crescents were retained brightly at congressed kinetochores (Figure 3E)
claims.evidence: This is observed in high-resolution time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: Astrin-4A-expressing cells displayed multiple blinking events within a short 60 s window.
claims.source: Unlike Astrin-WT-expressing cells, Astrin-4A-expressing cells displayed multiple blinking events within a short 60 s window, demonstrating compromised kinetochore life-time for YFP-Astrin-4A (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: The putative PP1-docking motif is essential for the maintenance of Astrin-crescents.
claims.source: We conclude that the putative PP1-docking motif is not essential for the initial arrival of Astrin sleeves at kinetochores; it is essential for the maintenance of Astrin-crescents
claims.evidence: This is concluded from observations of Astrin-4A dynamics at kinetochores.

claims.claim: Inter-kinetochore distances were significantly reduced in cells expressing Astrin-4A compared to Astrin-WT.
claims.source: Despite normal kinetochore alignment at the spindle equator, inter-kinetochore distances between Astrin crescents were significantly reduced in cells expressing Astrin-4A compared to Astrin-WT (Figure 3G).
claims.evidence: This is measured from live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: Average inter-kinetochore distances were significantly reduced in cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A compared to YFP-Astrin-WT.
claims.source: Measuring distances between CENP-B-DsRed pairs confirmed a significant reduction in average inter-kinetochore distances of cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A compared to YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B)
claims.evidence: This is measured from time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4B.

claims.claim: Taxol treatment induced no changes in the levels of YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70 at kinetochores.
claims.source: Taxol treatment induced no changes in the levels of YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70 at kinetochores (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through fixed-cell analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E.

claims.claim: Reduced microtubule-mediated pulling is a consequence, rather than the cause, of the reduced life-time of Astrin-4A at kinetochores.
claims.source: We conclude that reduced microtubule-mediated pulling is a consequence, rather than the cause, of the reduced life-time of Astrin-4A at kinetochores.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the observation that Taxol treatment does not rescue Astrin-4A localization.

claims.claim: PP1γ enriches at the outer-kinetochore.
claims.source: PP1γ enriches at the outer-kinetochore (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Cells co-expressing Astrin-CFP and YFP-PP1γ displayed prominent FRET signals only on those kinetochores that retained both Astrin-CFP and YFP-PP1γ.
claims.source: Cells co-expressing Astrin-CFP and YFP-PP1γ displayed prominent FRET signals only on those kinetochores that retained both Astrin-CFP and YFP-PP1γ (cyan arrow; Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is observed in FRET microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The C-terminus of Astrin and PP1γ are recruited at the kinetochore within a FRET distance of 5 nm between the CFP and YFP probes.
claims.source: These studies show that the C-terminus of Astrin and PP1γ are recruited at the kinetochore within a FRET distance of 5 nm between the CFP and YFP probes (Müller et al., 2013), suggesting a direct interaction between the tail of Astrin and PP1 at the outer kinetochore.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from FRET measurements and supported by citation to FRET methodology.

claims.claim: Astrin and PP1 interact at the outer-kinetochore, and this interaction is dynamic.
claims.source: We conclude that Astrin and PP1 interact at the outer-kinetochore, and this interaction is dynamic.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from FRET observations showing variable FRET signals at different kinetochores.

claims.claim: Astrin isoforms can interact with GST-PP1γ, but not GST, in Control siRNA treated mitotic cell lysates.
claims.source: Immunoblotting using anti-Astrin antibodies showed that Astrin isoforms can interact with GST-PP1γ, but not GST, in Control siRNA treated mitotic cell lysates, revealing a specific interaction between Astrin and PP1γ (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through pulldown assays shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Astrin interacts with GST-PP1γ, but not GST, in two independent repeats of recombinant protein purification and pull down experiments.
claims.source: Moreover, quantifying the ratio of Astrin band intensities in pull down lane relative to input lane of control siRNA treated cell lysates confirm that Astrin interacts with GST-PP1γ, but not GST, in two independent repeats of recombinant protein purification and pull down experiments (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from pulldown assay data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Astrin and PP1 interact with each other.
claims.source: In summary, in vivo FRET studies reveal a dynamic and spatially restricted interaction between Astrin and PP1 at kinetochores. In vitro pull-down studies show a specific interaction between GST-PP1 but not GST. Based on these in vivo and in vitro studies we conclude that Astrin and PP1 interact with each other.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from both FRET and pulldown experiments.

claims.claim: The Astrin-CFP 4A mutant expressing cells present severely reduced FRET signals compared to Astrin-WT expressing cells.
claims.source: However, using those timepoints when the Astrin-4A mutant was transiently enriched at the kinetochore, we could quantitatively establish that the Astrin-CFP 4A mutant expressing cells present severely reduced FRET signals compared to Astrin-WT expressing cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through FRET measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: The Astrin-CFP 4A mutant does not interact normally with YFP-PP1γ at kinetochores.
claims.source: These live-cell studies show that the Astrin-CFP 4A mutant does not interact normally with YFP-PP1γ at kinetochores.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from FRET measurements with the 4A mutant.

claims.claim: Cells expressing Astrin mutant (4A or ∆70) displayed significantly fewer end-on attached kinetochores compared to cells expressing Astrin-WT.
claims.source: Compared to cells expressing Astrin-WT, cells expressing Astrin mutant (4A or ∆70) displayed significantly fewer end-on attached kinetochores.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from attachment status analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Laterally-attached kinetochores, and not detached kinetochores, were significantly increased in Astrin mutant-expressing cells.
claims.source: Importantly, laterally-attached kinetochores, and not detached kinetochores, were significantly increased in Astrin mutant-expressing cells (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from attachment status analysis shown in Figure 5A,B.

claims.claim: Astrin mutant-expressing cells are able to retain kinetochores along microtubule-walls but they cannot maintain kinetochores at microtubule-ends.
claims.source: Thus, Astrin mutant-expressing cells are able to retain kinetochores along microtubule-walls but they cannot maintain kinetochores at microtubule-ends, similar to Astrin depleted cells (Shrestha et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is concluded from attachment status analysis and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: The kinetochore pool of Astrin is important for the selective stabilisation of end-on attachments.
claims.source: This reveals that the kinetochore pool of Astrin is important for the selective stabilisation of end-on attachments.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from observations that Astrin mutants fail to maintain end-on attachments.

claims.claim: The incidence of Astrin-crescents was dramatically reduced in monopolar spindles of cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70, compared to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT.
claims.source: In agreement, the incidence of Astrin-crescents was dramatically reduced in monopolar spindles of cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70, compared to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from monopolar spindle analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Astrin:PP1 interaction is required specifically to maintain end-on, but not lateral, attachments independent of biorientation status.
claims.source: These monopolar spindle studies together show that Astrin:PP1 interaction is required specifically to maintain end-on, but not lateral, attachments independent of biorientation status.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from monopolar spindle experiments showing selective defects in end-on attachments.

claims.claim: Astrin-mediated delivery of PP1 is not required for chromosome congression.
claims.source: Thus, although Astrin-mediated delivery of PP1 is not required for chromosome congression (Figure 2D,E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3C,D), it is crucial for the stable maintenance of end-on attachments (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is concluded from observations that Astrin mutants can congress chromosomes but fail to maintain end-on attachments.

claims.claim: Metaphase cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70 mutant displayed prominent Mad2 or ZW10 signals in a subset of congressed kinetochores.
claims.source: In contrast, metaphase cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70 mutant displayed prominent Mad2 or ZW10 signals in a subset of congressed kinetochores (Figure 5D,E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 5D,E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: There is an increased incidence of spindle checkpoint signalling in a small proportion of congressed kinetochores in cells expressing either of the two Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif.
claims.source: These data indicate an increased incidence of spindle checkpoint signalling in a small proportion of congressed kinetochores in cells expressing either of the two Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from checkpoint protein localization analysis.

claims.claim: Chromosome alignment at the spindle equator (i.e., congression efficiency) is not severely perturbed in Astrin mutant expressing cells.
claims.source: As expected from low resolution time-lapse studies (Figures 2 and 3), chromosome alignment at the spindle equator (i.e., congression efficiency) is not severely perturbed in Astrin mutant expressing cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through congression efficiency analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C.

claims.claim: The stable maintenance of end-on attachments, but not chromosome congression, requires the evolutionarily conserved PP1-docking motif in Astrin.
claims.source: Thus, the stable maintenance of end-on attachments, but not chromosome congression, requires the evolutionarily conserved PP1-docking motif in Astrin.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from multiple experimental observations with Astrin mutants.

claims.claim: The levels of DSN1 pSer100 are reduced at kinetochores in cells expressing Astrin WT compared to Astrin 4A or -∆70 mutant.
claims.source: Immunostaining of cells using phospho-specific antibodies against DSN1 pSer100 show that the levels of DSN1 pSer100 are reduced at kinetochores in cells expressing Astrin WT compared to Astrin 4A or -∆70 mutant (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: There is an increase in phosphorylated DSN1 signals in cells expressing Astrin 4A or -∆70 compared to Astrin WT.
claims.source: Quantitative analysis of phospho-signal positive kinetochores and integrated kinetochore signal intensities confirm an increase in phosphorylated DSN1 signals in cells expressing Astrin 4A or -∆70 compared to Astrin WT (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C.

claims.claim: Dsn1 phosphorylation status changes as a direct or indirect downstream target of Astrin-PP1 at kinetochores.
claims.source: These findings show changes in Dsn1 phosphorylation status as a direct or indirect downstream target of Astrin-PP1 at kinetochores.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from observations of DSN1 phosphorylation changes in Astrin mutant expressing cells.

claims.claim: Co-expressing mCherry-GBP-PP1γ fully rescued the kinetochore enrichment defect in both Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif.
claims.source: Nevertheless, co-expressing mCherry-GBP-PP1γ fully rescued the kinetochore enrichment defect in both Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif: both Astrin-∆70-GFP and Astrin-4A-GFP were enriched as bright crescents at the kinetochore when co-expressed with mCherry-GBP-PP1γ (Figure 6A,B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through rescue experiments shown in Figure 6A,B.

claims.claim: No rescue of the localisation defect was observed when Astrin-∆70 or −4A was fused to an N-terminal YFP tag in mCherry-GBP-PP1γ co-expressing cells.
claims.source: Importantly, no rescue of the localisation defect was observed when Astrin-∆70 or −4A was fused to an N-terminal YFP tag in mCherry-GBP-PP1γ co-expressing cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through rescue experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: The kinetochore enrichment of Astrin is dependent on spatially-defined delivery of PP1 phosphatase at Astrin's C-terminus.
claims.source: These studies show that the kinetochore enrichment of Astrin is dependent on spatially-defined delivery of PP1 phosphatase at Astrin's C-terminus (Figure 6C), which we show is proximal to the C-terminus of Ndc80 (Figure 1).
claims.evidence: This is concluded from rescue experiments showing position-dependent effects of PP1 delivery.

claims.claim: Cells co-expressing mCherry-GBP-PP1γ and Astrin-∆70-GFP or −4A-GFP display cold stable kinetochore-microtubule attachments.
claims.source: In contrast, cells co-expressing mCherry-GBP-PP1γ and Astrin-∆70-GFP or −4A-GFP display cold stable kinetochore-microtubule attachments, demonstrating a successful restoration of attachment stability in Astrin-∆70 or −4A mutant expressing cells by delivering PP1γ (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, right).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through cold stability assays shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The delivery of PP1 near the C-terminus of Ndc80 is sufficient to promote the kinetochore enrichment of Astrin-SKAP complex and stabilisation of end-on attachments.
claims.source: In summary, these findings show that the delivery of PP1 near the C-terminus of Ndc80 is sufficient to promote the kinetochore enrichment of Astrin-SKAP complex and stabilisation of end-on attachments (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is concluded from rescue experiments with GBP-PP1.

claims.claim: Depletion of Astrin did not abrogate SKA3 localisation at congressed kinetochores.
claims.source: Depletion of Astrin did not abrogate SKA3 localisation at congressed kinetochores (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: In Astrin -∆70 or −4A expressing cells, depleted of endogenous Astrin, SKA3 recruitment was unperturbed at congressed kinetochores.
claims.source: Similarly, in Astrin -∆70 or −4A expressing cells, depleted of endogenous Astrin, SKA3 recruitment was unperturbed at congressed kinetochores (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claims.claim: SKA complex enrichment is not linked to Astrin enrichment at the kinetochore.
claims.source: In conclusion, SKA complex enrichment is not linked to Astrin enrichment at the kinetochore.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from observations that SKA3 localizes normally in Astrin mutant expressing cells.

claims.claim: The failure to deliver PP1 by Astrin weakens KT-MT attachment stability without abrogating SKA complex recruitment at kinetochores.
claims.source: Thus, the failure to deliver PP1 by Astrin weakens KT-MT attachment stability without abrogating SKA complex recruitment at kinetochores.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from observations that Astrin mutants have attachment defects but normal SKA3 localization.

claims.claim: Despite the inhibition of Aurora-B, there was no kinetochore enrichment of 4A or ∆70 mutants in monopolar spindles.
claims.source: However, despite the inhibition of Aurora-B, there was no kinetochore enrichment of 4A or ∆70 mutants in monopolar spindles (Figure 7A,B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments combining Aurora-B inhibition with Astrin mutant expression shown in Figure 7A,B.

claims.claim: Aurora-B inhibited cells expressing Astrin-4A or -∆70 displayed a higher proportion of laterally-attached kinetochores compared to Astrin-WT expressing cells.
claims.source: In agreement, Aurora-B inhibited cells expressing Astrin-4A or -∆70 displayed a higher proportion of laterally-attached kinetochores compared to Astrin-WT expressing cells (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from attachment status analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Inhibiting Aurora-B does not stabilise end-on attachments in the absence of Astrin:PP1 interaction.
claims.source: These findings show that inhibiting Aurora-B does not stabilise end-on attachments in the absence of Astrin:PP1 interaction, showing the significance of Astrin:PP1 in stabilising KT-MT attachments.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that Aurora-B inhibition cannot rescue Astrin mutant defects.

claims.claim: Co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ rescued the kinetochore localisation defect of both mutants (Astrin-4A-GFP and Astrin-∆70-GFP) in monopolar spindles of cells treated with Aurora-B inhibitor.
claims.source: Co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ rescued the kinetochore localisation defect of both mutants (Astrin-4A-GFP and Astrin-∆70-GFP) in monopolar spindles of cells treated with Aurora-B inhibitor (compare Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through rescue experiments shown in Figure 7D,E.

claims.claim: The co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ increased the incidence of end-on attachments in Aurora-B inhibited cells expressing either Astrin-4A-GFP or Astrin-∆70-GFP.
claims.source: In addition, the co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ increased the incidence of end-on attachments in Aurora-B inhibited cells expressing either Astrin-4A-GFP or Astrin-∆70-GFP (Figure 7D; compare Figure 7F and C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from attachment status analysis shown in Figure 7D,F.

claims.claim: The stabilisation of end-on attachments following the inhibition of Aurora-B is acutely dependant on the delivery of PP1 by Astrin.
claims.source: These data show that the stabilisation of end-on attachments following the inhibition of Aurora-B is acutely dependant on the delivery of PP1 by Astrin.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that PP1 delivery is required even when Aurora-B is inhibited.

claims.claim: In the presence of Aurora-B activity (DMSO-treated cells), the co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ is insufficient to rescue both the kinetochore localisation and attachment defects of Astrin-4A-GFP or Astrin-∆70-GFP expressing cells.
claims.source: In the presence of Aurora-B activity (DMSO-treated cells), the co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ is insufficient to rescue both the kinetochore localisation and attachment defects of Astrin-4A-GFP or Astrin-∆70-GFP expressing cells (Figure 7E,F and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C)
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments shown in Figure 7E,F.

claims.claim: Both Astrin-PP1 and Aurora-B control KT-MT attachment status.
claims.source: showing that both Astrin-PP1 and Aurora-B control KT-MT attachment status
claims.evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that both Aurora-B inhibition and PP1 delivery are required for attachment stability.

claims.claim: Cells depleted of endogenous Astrin and expressing Astrin-WT-GFP disassembled monopolar asters normally to build bipolar spindles within 2 hr after STLC-release.
claims.source: When STLC and Aurora-B inhibiting drugs were washed off, cells depleted of endogenous Astrin and expressing Astrin-WT-GFP, disassembled monopolar asters normally to build bipolar spindles within 2 hr (Figure 8A,B).
claims.evidence: This is observed in time-lapse microscopy experiments shown in Figure 8A,B.

claims.claim: 45 min after STLC-release, cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed Astrin-WT-GFP enrichment on paired kinetochores.
claims.source: In contrast, 45 min after STLC-release, cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed Astrin-WT-GFP enrichment on paired kinetochores (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E)
claims.evidence: This is observed in fixed-cell analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Greater than 60% of Astrin depleted cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed unaligned chromosomes.
claims.source: Importantly, time-lapse movies showed that greater than 60% of Astrin depleted cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed unaligned chromosomes (Figure 8A; n = 56 cells)
claims.evidence: This is quantified from time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 8A.

claims.claim: ~54% of anaphase cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed lagging chromosomes and a delayed anaphase onset.
claims.source: and ~54% of anaphase cells displayed lagging chromosomes and a delayed anaphase onset (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B,C,D; n = 24 cells)
claims.evidence: This is quantified from time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B,C,D.

claims.claim: There is a need for a dynamic interaction between Astrin and PP1.
claims.source: These observations highlight the need for a dynamic interaction between Astrin and PP1.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from observations that constitutive PP1 delivery causes defects.

claims.claim: Astrin-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ co-expressing cells were significantly delayed in congressing chromosomes compared to Astrin-GFP alone expressing cells.
claims.source: Analysing the rate of chromosome congression in cells presenting clear monopolar spindles showed that Astrin-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ co-expressing cells were significantly delayed in congressing chromosomes compared to Astrin-GFP alone expressing cells (Figure 8C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 8C.

claims.claim: The constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin disrupts the dynamic regulation of attachment stability leading to a delay in chromosome congression and anaphase onset and also errors in chromosome segregation.
claims.source: These findings show that the constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin disrupts the dynamic regulation of attachment stability leading to a delay in chromosome congression and anaphase onset and also errors in chromosome segregation.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from experiments with constitutive PP1 delivery.

claims.claim: Two important sequential steps drive the rapid and selective stabilisation of end-on attachments: first, the reduction of Aurora-B activity allows the formation of end-on attachments and the initial recruitment of Astrin-sleeves at the kinetochore. Next, Astrin-mediated delivery of PP1, near the C-terminus of Ndc80, promotes its own enrichment as Astrin-crescents.
claims.source: In summary, two important sequential steps drive the rapid and selective stabilisation of end-on attachments: first, the reduction of Aurora-B activity allows the formation of end-on attachments and the initial recruitment of Astrin-sleeves at the kinetochore. Next, Astrin-mediated delivery of PP1, near the C-terminus of Ndc80, promotes its own enrichment as Astrin-crescents - this positive feedback stabilises end-on attachments to withstand microtubule-mediated pulling (Figure 9).
claims.evidence: This is the main mechanistic conclusion summarized from all experimental observations and illustrated in Figure 9.

claims.claim: Although the inhibition of Aurora-B is essential for the formation of end-on attachment, it is insufficient to stabilise attachments in the absence of Astrin-mediated PP1 delivery.
claims.source: Although the inhibition of Aurora-B is essential for the formation of end-on attachment, it is insufficient to stabilise attachments in the absence of Astrin-mediated PP1 delivery.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that Aurora-B inhibition cannot rescue Astrin mutant defects.

claims.claim: Constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin disrupts the dynamic regulation of KT-MT attachment stability causing delayed chromosome congression and defective anaphase.
claims.source: Conversely, constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin disrupts the dynamic regulation of KT-MT attachment stability causing delayed chromosome congression and defective anaphase.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from experiments with constitutive PP1 delivery.

claims.claim: Astrin-PP1 interaction acts as a dynamic lock that rapidly and selectively stabilises mature kinetochore-microtubule attachments to ensure the accurate segregation of chromosomes.
claims.source: Thus, Astrin-PP1 interaction acts as a dynamic lock that rapidly and selectively stabilises mature kinetochore-microtubule attachments to ensure the accurate segregation of chromosomes.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on all experimental observations.

results.result: Astrin is recruited to end-on attached kinetochores in two distinct forms (sleeves and crescents) prior to biorientation, with the C-terminus of Astrin positioned within 5 nm of the C-terminus of Ndc80 as demonstrated by FRET microscopy.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C29 provide converging evidence from live-cell imaging (C24-C26) and FRET microscopy (C27-C28) demonstrating Astrin's spatial organization at kinetochores. The FRET data with appropriate controls (C28) and colocalization with outer-kinetochore markers (C26) provide strong support for the specific positioning of Astrin's C-terminus near Ndc80's C-terminus.

results.result: The C-terminal 70 amino acid tail of Astrin (1123-1193 a.a.) is essential for Astrin enrichment as crescents at kinetochores and for timely anaphase onset, but is dispensable for bipolar spindle maintenance and chromosome congression.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C40 demonstrate through deletion mutagenesis that the Astrin tail is specifically required for kinetochore enrichment (C32-C33) but not spindle bipolarity (C35-C36). Time-lapse microscopy data (C37-C38) show functional consequences (delayed anaphase) without affecting congression, providing strong evidence for a specific role in attachment stabilization rather than general mitotic functions.

results.result: A conserved PP1-docking RVxF motif in Astrin's C-terminal tail is critical for Astrin enrichment at kinetochores and timely anaphase onset, but dispensable for spindle bipolarity and chromosome congression.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C49 provide strong evidence through bioinformatic identification (C41-C42), point mutagenesis (C43-C45), and functional assays (C46-C49). The 4A mutant phenocopies the Δ70 deletion mutant in key respects, supporting the importance of the PP1-docking motif. Multiple independent assays (localization, timing, congression) provide converging evidence.

results.result: The PP1-docking motif is essential for maintaining stable Astrin-crescents at kinetochores, as demonstrated by increased 'blinking' events (transient loss of Astrin signal) in cells expressing the Astrin-4A mutant.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C53 use high-resolution time-lapse imaging to demonstrate dynamic instability of Astrin-4A at kinetochores. The quantification of blinking events (C52) provides objective evidence for reduced kinetochore lifetime. This directly supports the conclusion that the PP1-docking motif maintains, rather than initiates, Astrin recruitment.

results.result: Cells expressing Astrin-4A mutant show reduced inter-kinetochore distances indicative of reduced microtubule-mediated pulling forces, and this is a consequence rather than cause of reduced Astrin stability at kinetochores.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C57 demonstrate reduced inter-kinetochore distances using two independent markers (Astrin crescents and CENP-B). The Taxol experiment (C56-C57) provides critical evidence for causality by showing that stabilizing microtubules does not rescue Astrin-4A localization, supporting the interpretation that attachment instability causes reduced pulling rather than vice versa.

results.result: Astrin and PP1γ interact dynamically at the outer-kinetochore, as demonstrated by FRET microscopy in live cells and GST-pulldown assays with mitotic cell lysates.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C64 provide both in vivo (FRET) and in vitro (pulldown) evidence for Astrin-PP1 interaction. The FRET data show spatial proximity (<5 nm) and dynamic behavior (C61), while pulldown assays (C62-C63) demonstrate specific biochemical interaction. The convergence of two independent methods strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: The Astrin-4A mutant shows severely reduced FRET signals with YFP-PP1γ compared to wild-type Astrin, indicating disrupted interaction at kinetochores.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C66 demonstrate that mutation of the RVxF motif disrupts Astrin-PP1 interaction using FRET. The analysis appropriately accounts for the transient nature of Astrin-4A localization by analyzing timepoints when the mutant is present. This provides direct evidence linking the RVxF motif to PP1 binding.

results.result: Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif (4A and Δ70) specifically fail to maintain end-on kinetochore-microtubule attachments while retaining lateral attachments, independent of biorientation status as demonstrated in monopolar spindles.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C73 use quantitative attachment status analysis in monopolar spindles to demonstrate selective defects in end-on attachment maintenance. The monopolar spindle system (C71-C72) is crucial for demonstrating biorientation-independence. The specific increase in lateral attachments without increased detachment (C68) supports a selective defect in end-on attachment stabilization rather than general attachment defects.

results.result: Cells expressing Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif show increased spindle checkpoint signaling (Mad2 and ZW10) at a subset of congressed kinetochores, despite normal chromosome congression efficiency.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C77 demonstrate checkpoint activation using two independent markers (Mad2 and ZW10) in metaphase cells with congressed chromosomes. The observation that only a subset of kinetochores show checkpoint activation (C75) is consistent with the dynamic nature of attachment defects. The normal congression efficiency (C76) confirms that the checkpoint activation is not due to gross alignment defects.

results.result: DSN1 phosphorylation at Ser100 is increased at kinetochores in cells expressing Astrin mutants (4A or Δ70) compared to wild-type, indicating altered phosphorylation status as a downstream consequence of disrupted Astrin-PP1 function.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 demonstrate increased DSN1 phosphorylation using phospho-specific antibodies with both qualitative and quantitative analysis. However, the claim appropriately acknowledges uncertainty about whether DSN1 is a direct or indirect target (C80). This provides evidence for functional consequences of Astrin-PP1 disruption but does not establish mechanism.

results.result: Artificially tethering PP1γ to the C-terminus, but not N-terminus, of Astrin mutants rescues both kinetochore enrichment and attachment stability, demonstrating that spatially-restricted PP1 delivery near Ndc80's C-terminus is sufficient for Astrin function.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C85 provide strong rescue evidence using GBP-mediated PP1 tethering. The position-dependence (C82) is critical for demonstrating spatial specificity. The rescue of both localization (C81) and function (C84, cold stability) provides strong evidence that PP1 delivery is the key function of the Astrin tail. This is a well-designed rescue experiment with appropriate controls.

results.result: SKA complex recruitment to kinetochores is independent of Astrin enrichment, as SKA3 localizes normally in cells depleted of Astrin or expressing Astrin mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C89 demonstrate that SKA3 localization is unaffected by Astrin depletion or mutation. This is important for establishing that Astrin-PP1 has a distinct role from SKA-PP1 in attachment stabilization. The use of SKA3 as a readout for the complex is appropriate given its established role as a complex component.

results.result: Inhibiting Aurora-B kinase is insufficient to stabilize end-on attachments in the absence of Astrin-PP1 interaction, but PP1 delivery by Astrin requires Aurora-B inhibition to stabilize attachments, demonstrating that both pathways are required for attachment stability.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C97 provide strong evidence that Astrin-PP1 and Aurora-B pathways are both required for attachment stability through epistasis experiments. The demonstration that Aurora-B inhibition cannot rescue Astrin mutant defects (C90-C92) is critical for establishing that Astrin-PP1 is not simply reversing Aurora-B phosphorylation. The rescue by GBP-PP1 only in Aurora-B inhibited cells (C93-C95) demonstrates the requirement for both pathways.

results.result: Constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin (through GBP-PP1 co-expression) disrupts chromosome congression and segregation, causing unaligned chromosomes, lagging chromosomes, and delayed anaphase, demonstrating the requirement for dynamic Astrin-PP1 interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C104 demonstrate that constitutive PP1 delivery causes defects using monopolar-to-bipolar spindle conversion assays. The observation of multiple defects (congression delay C103, lagging chromosomes C101, unaligned chromosomes C100) provides strong evidence that dynamic regulation is required. This is important for establishing that Astrin-PP1 is not simply a constitutive stabilizer but requires temporal regulation.

results.result: Astrin-PP1 acts as a dynamic 'lock' that selectively and rapidly stabilizes end-on kinetochore-microtubule attachments through a positive feedback mechanism: PP1 delivery by Astrin promotes Astrin's own enrichment, which stabilizes attachments independent of biorientation, and this process requires both Aurora-B inhibition and dynamic Astrin-PP1 interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C11 and C105-C108 represent the main conclusions synthesized from all experimental observations. The evidence for positive feedback (C5), biorientation-independence (C6), requirement for both Aurora-B and Astrin-PP1 (C8, C106), spatial specificity (C9), and need for dynamic regulation (C10, C107) is well-supported by the grouped experimental results. The 'dynamic lock' model (C11, C108) appropriately integrates all findings.

results.result: Background knowledge claims establish that microtubules segregate chromosomes through kinetochore attachments, only end-on attachments can generate pulling forces, and checkpoint proteins prevent premature segregation in the absence of proper attachments.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C2 and C12-C16 represent established knowledge in the field supported by appropriate citations to review articles and primary literature. These provide necessary context for the study but are not novel findings. The claims are accurately stated and appropriately cited.

results.result: Prior work establishes that Aurora-B destabilizes attachments through Ndc80 phosphorylation, KNL1-recruited PP1 is not essential for attachment stability, checkpoint proteins are removed when end-on attachments form, Astrin-SKAP is recruited to end-on attached kinetochores, and Astrin-SKAP depletion disrupts stable maintenance of end-on attachments.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C23 accurately summarize prior work with appropriate citations. These establish the rationale for investigating Astrin-PP1 as a distinct mechanism from KNL1-PP1 (C18-C19) and provide context for the current findings. The claims are accurately attributed to cited work.

results.result: Bioinformatic analysis identifies a conserved PP1-docking RVxF motif in the C-terminal tail of Astrin across Bilateria, suggesting evolutionary conservation of this mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C42 demonstrate evolutionary conservation through sequence analysis. The identification of the RVxF motif (C41) is supported by comparison to known PP1-docking motifs in KNL1. The extension to other Bilateria (C42) provides evidence for functional importance through evolutionary conservation. However, the bioinformatic analysis would benefit from more detailed description of methods and statistical significance.
